E076-01.notes: Interrupting 'however' between subject and verb needs paired commas: 'Brewster, however, earned little.' A leaves the closing comma off, so the subject and verb get split. B puts a semicolon after 'Brewster', which leaves a fragment ('Brewster;'). D puts a semicolon between 'however' and 'earned', which splits the subject from its verb. Only one option is defensible. The stray errors elsewhere in the passage (S2 'was repeated', S4 comma splice, S6 'was sold') belong to other items and do not affect this one.
